section_1.title: The Problem: Information Overload
section_1.content: Introduce the limitation of previous models (RNNs) that process word-by-word, often forgetting the beginning of a long sentence. We need a way to look at the 'whole picture' at once.
section_1.example: Reading a long mystery novel and trying to remember the character introduced on page 1 while on page 100.

section_2.title: Intuitive Concept: The Spotlight
section_2.content: Explain 'Attention' as a spotlight. Instead of looking at everything with equal focus, the model assigns different weights to different parts of the input based on relevance.
section_2.example: When hearing the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired', you naturally focus on 'animal' when reading 'it'.

section_3.title: The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values
section_3.content: Define the math components: Query (what I'm looking for), Key (what I have to offer), and Value (the actual information). Use a visual analogy of a library search system.
section_3.example: A student (Query) searches the library catalog (Keys) to find the relevant content (Value) in a specific book.

section_4.title: Mathematical Visualization (Softmax)
section_4.content: Explain the dot-product calculation followed by Softmax. Visually represent this as a 'Heat Map' grid where intensity levels show the strength of connections between words.
section_4.example: Imagine a 3x3 grid where 'The' + 'Animal' yields a high-intensity color block, indicating a strong syntactic relationship.

section_5.title: Synthesis: Putting it All Together
section_5.content: Summarize how these calculations allow the Transformer to create 'context-aware' word representations that capture deep meanings and long-range dependencies.
section_5.example: Finalizing the model: A robot assistant successfully disambiguating 'bank' (river vs. money) by scanning the entire paragraph's context weights.

section_1.title: The Problem: Information Overload
section_1.content: Introduce the limitation of previous models (RNNs) that process word-by-word, often forgetting the beginning of a long sentence. We need a way to look at the 'whole picture' at once.
section_1.example: Reading a long mystery novel and trying to remember the character introduced on page 1 while on page 100.

section_2.title: Intuitive Concept: The Spotlight
section_2.content: Explain 'Attention' as a spotlight. Instead of looking at everything with equal focus, the model assigns different weights to different parts of the input based on relevance.
section_2.example: When hearing the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired', you naturally focus on 'animal' when reading 'it'.

section_3.title: The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values
section_3.content: Define the math components: Query (what I'm looking for), Key (what I have to offer), and Value (the actual information). Use a visual analogy of a library search system.

section_4.title: Mathematical Visualization (Softmax)
section_4.content: Explain the dot-product calculation followed by Softmax. Visually represent this as a 'Heat Map' grid where intensity levels show the strength of connections between words.
section_4.example: Imagine a 3x3 grid where 'The' + 'Animal' yields a high-intensity color block, indicating a strong syntactic relationship.

section_5.title: Synthesis: Putting it All Together
section_5.content: Summarize how these calculations allow the Transformer to create 'context-aware' word representations that capture deep meanings and long-range dependencies.
section_5.example: Finalizing the model: A robot assistant successfully disambiguating 'bank' (river vs. money) by scanning the entire paragraph's context weights.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
